messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: KV cache memory fragmentation spike detected on gpu-pool-dedicated-3. Alerting on sustained per-process CUDA RSS growth + vma churn.
oncall-bot: Incident severity: high. Affected service: inference-runtime.kv-cache. Potential customer impact: elevated latency / 502s for some requests.
mike: I'm seeing continuous-batching throughput jump at 02:04 UTC and then steady GPU allocator growth. Logs show repeated `cudaMalloc` retries + fragmentation warnings.
nana: tagging infra: @liam @eva — can we get a quick triage? Which hosts are hottest?
eva: grabbing flamegraphs and pmap dumps now. initial list: gpu-pool-dedicated-3 instances i-0a12, i-0b34 showing arena fragmentation.
liam: hypothesis: an optimizer change in the last rollout increased batch growth factor; that pushed larger KV cache allocations and triggered many small allocations, which leads to pt malloc fragmentation on 22.x driver.
mike: correlates with deploy 2102341000 (continuous-batching v2.3.1).
sarah: CS: two customers reported slow responses and a 15s tail latency spike, one issued a partial rollback on their side. They're asking if it's infra-side.
eva: heap snapshot from i-0a12 (snip):
```
Allocator arenas: 8
Largest free chunk: 1.2MB
Total allocated (process): 19.3GB
Slab fragmentation: ~22%
Freed-but-not-returned: 4.8GB
backtrace top: kv_cache::store_prefix, continuous_batch::append_request
```
mike: confirmed pyro/pytorch malloc patterns: many small-ish cached fragments, few large contiguous frees. Classic fragmentation.
liam: mitigation plan: 1) reduce continuous-batching max_growth to previous value 2) trigger manual compaction on affected pools (force free arenas or restart worker) 3) short-term rollback of v2.3.1->v2.3.0 if needed.
nana: can we do a config hotfix (no full deploy) to change batching growth and cache sizing? That would be fastest.
eva: yes. We can flip runtime-config via the control plane. I'll prepare the curl.
liam: please include a safety circuit to avoid oscillation. set max_growth=1.2 -> from 2.0 and set per-process kv_cache_limit=16GB.
mike: monitoring queries:
```
# track per-host gpu rss growth
sum by (instance) (max_over_time(process_gpu_rss_bytes[5m]))
```
and
```
# count of cudaMalloc failures
sum(rate(cuda_malloc_retries_total[1m]))
```
we should watch those.
sarah: I notified the two affected customers and asked for any traces; told them we're rolling a hotfix. they appreciate the quick heads-up.
eva: executing hotpatch now:
```bash
curl -X POST https://controlplane.redwood.internal/configs/runtime-change \ 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $CP_TOKEN' \ 
  -d '{"service":"inference-runtime","continuous_batching.max_growth":1.2,"kv_cache.per_process_limit_bytes":"17179869184"}'
```
(replaced token in chat)
ops-bot: Received config change, validating constraints...
ops-bot: Rolling change to gpu-pool-dedicated* (batching config only) -> 200 nodes planned, concurrency 10.
deploy-bot: Deploy step 1/4: pushing config to control plane (in progress)
mike: I'm seeing drops in cudaMalloc retry rate starting ~40s after patch. good signal.
liam: also kick compaction on the worst hosts to reclaim fragmented regions:
```bash
ssh ops@gpu-pool-dedicated-3-i-0a12 'pkill -USR1 inference-worker && sleep 5 && systemctl restart inference-worker'
```
(this causes KV cache to flush with an orderly compaction)
eva: started compaction on i-0a12, i-0b34, i-0c56 sequentially to avoid global throughput hits.
nana: operational note: compaction restarts will briefly reduce throughput for that host; routing will shift traffic. we've scheduled sequential restarts to keep SLOs intact.
sarah: CS update: customer A sees latency back to baseline, customer B reports reduced errors. they still want a timeline.
liam: next steps: continue monitoring for 30m. if any host still growing, escalate to full rollback of continuous-batching service -> coordinate with deployments.
mike: graphs look better. cudaMalloc retries nearly 0. per-host RSS flattened.
ops-bot: Config rollout: 200/200 nodes updated. No errors.
deploy-bot: Step 4/4: post-rollout verification passed.
eva: compaction finished on the three worst hosts. memory reclaimed ~3.8GB total on those.
nana: thanks team. start drafting incident summary. assign postmortem owners: ana (incident lead), liam (allocator/root cause), eva (mitigation playbook updates), mike (monitoring + alerts tuning), sarah (customer comms).
nana: oncall shift ending in 35m. handing off to @liam. please take over and continue watch. mention if you need rotation.
liam: taking over watch. will keep 1-hour high-sensitivity window then move to normal.
mike: note for postmortem: add metric for continuous-batch growth factor and a synthetic that simulates allocation shape to catch frag-prone patterns.
sarah: CS followup: customers onboarded to incident channel, asked for postmortem and compensatory credits if SLA breached.
nana: thanks again. closing pager for now; reopen if any regressions. :white_check_mark:
liam: acknowledging handoff. creating a follow-up ticket: RFC-2102345678: allocator-tuning-and-compact-api.
nana: tagging in the doc: https://redwood.internal/incidents/2102345678 (will be updated with timelines and diag)
liam: quick reminder: schedule a canary for the fixed batching config next deploy and include an allocator-stress test.
nana: end of thread.
